tools.name: submit_log
tools.description:
Submit a tamper-evident log entry to TrustNotch.

        Provide EXACTLY ONE of:
          - payload: a JSON object to record (TrustNotch canonicalizes, hashes, stores it), or
          - content_hash: a 64-char lowercase hex SHA-256 you computed locally
            (zero-PII mode — the underlying content is never sent).
        Returns the receipt: id, content_hash, created_at, receipt_signature, receipt_key_id.

tools.name: get_log
tools.description: Fetch a previously submitted log entry by its id (a UUID string).

tools.name: get_proof
tools.description:
Fetch the tamper-evident proof bundle for a log entry (a UUID string).

        The bundle has the signed receipt, the Merkle inclusion proof, and the
        OpenTimestamps Bitcoin anchor. A just-submitted entry may not be batched yet —
        you'll get a 'not available yet' message; retry in ~60s.

tools.name: verify_proof
tools.description:
Verify a TrustNotch proof bundle locally, offline — server not trusted.

        Pass a bundle previously returned by get_proof. Independently recomputes the
        leaf hash and Merkle root and checks three tiers: receipt (Ed25519 signature),
        inclusion (RFC 6962), and anchor_structural (the OpenTimestamps Bitcoin anchor).
        Trusted keys come from GET /v1/keys, or from a pinned local file when
        TRUSTNOTCH_PUBKEYS_PATH is set (stronger independence). 'trusted_keys_source'
        records which was used. If keys are unavailable, the keyless tiers (inclusion +
        anchor) are still checked and 'receipt' is reported as 'na' with a warning.

tools.name: verify_log
tools.description:
Fetch a log entry's proof and verify it locally in one step.

        Convenience over get_proof + verify_proof. Returns the per-tier verification
        result, or a 'not available yet' / 'not found' message if the proof can't be
        fetched (e.g. the entry isn't batched yet).
